speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please describe the skin lesions and tell me when they first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the daycare exposure and similar lesions in another child, these are likely molluscum contagiosum. Can you describe the appearance of the papules, specifically if they are dome-shaped with a central dimple or umbilication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of pearly, umbilicated papules is pathognomonic for molluscum contagiosum, so no further testing is needed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
